subject: Request: Clarify training exclusion, prompt/response IP & subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@novamed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2027-05-16T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify training exclusion + prompt/response IP and subprocessors

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we're moving toward a pilot, Legal has a few outstanding asks specific to how Redwood will handle our conversational data:

- We need a firm contractual commitment that Novamed data will not be used to train or improve models (including fine-tuning or selective retraining). Please point to the exact clause you propose.
- For auditability, can you provide a mechanism or export that proves prompt/response provenance for a given session (timestamps, model variant, request/response hashes)?
- Novamed requires a subprocessors inventory and a short attestation that any cross-border subprocessors will not use our data for training.
- Finally, our legal team is asking whether Redwood is willing to place customer prompts/responses into an escrow or custody workflow in the event of a long-term dispute over derivative rights.

We'd like to resolve these items before sending a PO. Can you send a short written response and any artifacts (DPA language, inventory, ops playbook) by EOD Tuesday?

Best,
Samira
Chief Privacy Officer
Novamed

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-16T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training exclusion + prompt/response IP and subprocessors

Samira —

Thanks for laying this out clearly. Short answers up front, then attachments and next steps below.

High level (summary):
- Training exclusion: Redwood can contractually commit to not use customer data (prompts/responses) to train or improve our models for Novamed-specific datasets. We propose a DPA addendum clause we call the "Model Improvement Exclusion" that explicitly prevents retention for training, and we have an operational control (a runtime flag and an isolation lane) that enforces this at the serving layer.
- Prompt/response provenance: We can export an audit package that includes request/response metadata (timestamps, model variant, token counts, and a content hash). Raw full-response exports are possible under the same export process but subject to retention and privacy redaction rules.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor inventory and a one-page attestation we provide for customers; we also offer onshore routing (US-only) for sensitive traffic on request.
- Escrow/custody for prompts/responses: We don't typically escrow live prompt/response data, but we can offer contractual remedies and an operational path to deliver an evidence snapshot or archive to an agreed custodian under narrow conditions.

I've attached: 1) a proposed DPA addendum (redline-friendly PDF), 2) the subprocessor inventory, and 3) an ops playbook describing the no-training lane.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call to walk the redlines and confirm scope. I'm available Tue 5/18 10:00–11:30 PT or Wed 5/19 14:00–16:00 PT. Ben and Laura are looped for procurement and legal specifics.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redline_Novamed_v1.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_202705.pdf; operational_playbook_no_training.pdf

From: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@novamed.com>, procurement@novamed.com
Date: 2027-05-17T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training exclusion + prompt/response IP and subprocessors (redlines)

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. We reviewed the DPA addendum and have a few redline-level items we'd like to discuss:

1) Escrow / custody: we propose a stronger contractual mechanism that allows Novamed to require delivery of a full session archive (prompts + responses + provenance metadata) to an agreed neutral escrow provider if Redwood materially changes ownership or business model, or if there's a long dispute over derivative rights.
2) Derivative rights: the current language preserves customer ownership of prompts/responses, but we need clarity on downstream "derivatives" — Novamed needs confirmation that any model outputs derived using our prompts or responses (beyond the immediate response to our API call) will not be asserted as Redwood IP and must be covered by a nonexclusive license back to Novamed.
3) Subprocessors and cross-border: please confirm which subprocessors have access to raw conversational payloads and provide the last SOC report for any subprocessor that handles plaintext. We also need the attestation you mentioned in writing (signed).

I've attached a redlined version of your addendum (DPA_redline_Novamed_v1.pdf) with markups and a list of specific clause language we'd like to see. Can your legal team propose language on items (1) and (2)?

Regards,
Maya Hargreaves
Senior Counsel
Novamed

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Novamed Legal <legal@novamed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@novamed.com>
Date: 2027-05-18T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify training exclusion + prompt/response IP and subprocessors (redlines)

Maya / Samira —

Appreciate the detailed feedback. Below are direct responses to each of your redline items and a proposed operational stance we can include in the addendum. If helpful, Laura from our legal team can draft explicit language for the DPA addendum after we align on the mechanics.

1) Escrow / custody:
- Contractual option: We can add a clause allowing Novamed to require delivery of a session archive to a mutually agreed neutral custodian under limited triggers (change of control, insolvency, or a defined material IP dispute). This would be scoped to the customer tenant and restricted to data for the specified timeframe.
- Operational path: We will produce an export bundle (prompts, responses, provenance metadata, model variant, timestamps, and content hashes) in an encrypted archive. Delivery will be to the agreed escrow provider, with a PKI-signed manifest.

2) Derivative rights:
- Ownership: Novamed retains ownership of prompts and verbatim responses.
- Derivatives: Redwood will not claim ownership of downstream derivative works that are solely based on Novamed-provided prompts/responses. Our standard position is to grant customers a perpetual, royalty-free license to outputs and derivatives produced from their data. We can add a clause making that explicit for Novamed.

3) Subprocessors and cross-border:
- Inventory: see attached subprocessor_inventory_202705.pdf (current as of 2027-05-01).
- Access: only a subset of subprocessors handle plaintext request/response payloads (listed in the inventory). For those, we can provide the most recent SOC/TAC reports under NDA; we will deliver the attestation signed by our Head of Security confirming that Novamed tenant traffic is not used for model training.
- Onshore routing: we can route traffic to US-only processing lanes where the customer requests (operational and pricing details to follow).

4) Prompt/response provenance & exports:
- Audit export: we can provide a time-bound export containing metadata and optionally the content; exports include model variant, timestamps, request/response hash, and token counts. Full content exports are subject to retention windows and privacy redaction.

Next steps:
- Laura to draft DPA addendum language for 1–3 above and circulate a clean version plus a companion operational SOW describing export format, retention SLAs, and escrow process.
- Proposed call: Thu 2027-05-20 10:00 PT to walk redlines and confirm the escrow trigger definitions.

Thanks — we aim to get a clean addendum you can sign without changing your product use.

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: DPA_redline_Novamed_v1.pdf; subprocessor_inventory_202705.pdf; operational_playbook_no_training.pdf
